title: I am the resurrection (John 11:1–27)
hook: Martha meets him on the road and makes her confession

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hanukkah in winter, under Solomon's porch, and a promise about hands that won't let go. Your line was no one can snatch them. Who did you send a message to? Day six hundred twenty-two.

A message arrives across the Jordan from two sisters in Bethany, a village just outside Jerusalem. It's short, and it doesn't ask for anything directly: "Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick." Their brother Lazarus. The one you love. John adds, so we can't miss it: "Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus." And then the strangest sentence. Right after telling us he loved them, John says that when Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was two more days. John doesn't explain the wait. Not yet.

When Jesus finally says, let's go back to Judea, the disciples are alarmed. They tried to stone you there. Thomas, the one later remembered for doubting, says something brave and bleak: "Let us also go, that we may die with him." By the time they reach Bethany, Lazarus has been in the tomb four days. Friends have come from Jerusalem to comfort the sisters. And Martha, hearing Jesus is near, doesn't wait at home. She goes out to meet him on the road. Her first words are honest, almost an accusation: "Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died." Then, in the same breath, she says she knows God will give him whatever he asks. Jesus says: your brother will rise again. Martha answers with a hope she already holds, a resurrection of the dead at the end of time: "I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day." Someday. Far off. And Jesus brings it into the present tense: "I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live." Not, there will be a resurrection. I am. Then he asks her directly: believest thou this? And Martha makes her confession: "Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world." In Matthew's Gospel, it's Peter who says something like this. In John, it's Martha, standing on a road, grieving, with her brother four days in the tomb.
screen: then, large: `I AM THE RESURRECTION, AND THE LIFE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say what you believe out loud. Settle, and breathe. Martha said two things at once: if you had been here, and I believe. Grief and faith in the same breath. Think about what you actually believe today, whatever it is. It might be about God. It might be simpler: that love matters, that people can change, that the person you lost still matters. Find one sentence that's true for you. Then, quietly, say it out loud. Hear your own voice say it. If you pray, you can say it to God, the way Martha did. If you don't, say it to the room. The bell holds the time.
I am the resurrection. One of Jesus's I am sayings in John, spoken to Martha on the road, with her brother four days in the tomb.
Your line: I am the resurrection. Today, if grief or disappointment comes up, let it sit beside what you believe, the way Martha held both on the road. Day six hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Jesus's words to Martha are often read at Christian funerals; in the Book of Common Prayer burial service, they are the first words said as the body is brought to the church.

original.note: Greek: resurrection, literally a standing up again.

trapdoor: what you thought: a promise about heaven someday.
what it means: Martha believes in a resurrection far off, and Jesus says: I am the resurrection, here, now.
what a scholar hears: anastasis, standing up again; and Martha's confession echoes Peter's in Matthew.

notes: 'Many Jews of her day believed in a resurrection of the dead at the end of time' (Pharisees did; Sadducees did not). Confirm phrasing.
Burial service opening sentence 'I am the resurrection and the life' (Book of Common Prayer and many others): howItsDone says 'in many churches'. Confirm.
Hook softened in review: 'Because he loved them... he stayed' read a causal link into 11:5–6 ('therefore' in KJV 11:6 is debated); now 'Right after telling us he loved them'. Confirm.
Count of I am sayings: resurrection as fifth (bread, light, door, shepherd, resurrection). Confirm consistency.

Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer tells the listener what they feel; cut 'many Jews of her day' (Martha's own words carry it), the 'fifth I am saying' count (voice, word, trapdoor), 'one of the great confessions', and 'among the most read at funerals'; the Peter parallel now names Matthew.
